# HTTP API

Extracted from the `router()` functions in `src/handlers/`, with each
endpoint's prose taken from the `///` on its handler. Nothing here is
hand-maintained, so it cannot drift from the routers it describes.

Error bodies are the one shape in `src/errors.rs`; status codes are stated
in each handler's doc where they are part of the contract.

## `handlers::admin`

Admin routes: users/roles, coupons CRUD, feature toggles + runtime settings,
stats, moderation (reviews/feedback), and the ops-token surface (the legacy
and media migrations + per-version stats/feedbacks).

### `GET /api/admin/coupons`

Admin coupon list, newest first, each with derived status + usage.

Handler: `handlers::admin::list_coupons_handler`

### `POST /api/admin/coupons`

Create a coupon. 400 on any invalid field, 409 on a duplicate code.

Handler: `handlers::admin::create_coupon_handler`

### `GET /api/admin/coupons/{coupon_id}`

One coupon with usage (admin editor).

Handler: `handlers::admin::get_coupon_handler`

### `POST /api/admin/coupons/{coupon_id}/save`

Save every editable field of a coupon (identity and created_at preserved;
the redemption log is untouched, so usage stats survive edits and pauses).

Handler: `handlers::admin::save_coupon_handler`

### `POST /api/admin/coupons/{coupon_id}/delete`

Delete a coupon and its redemption log. Already-granted quests stay owned
(«удаление необратимо; уже применённые скидки сохраняются»).

Handler: `handlers::admin::delete_coupon_handler`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::admin::list_users_handler`

### `POST /api/admin/users/{user_id}/role`

Assign a role to a registered account. Admin-gated, with three guards:
* an unknown role value → 400 ([`auth::validate_role`]);
* a session-admin changing THEIR OWN role → 409 (prevents accidental
self-lockout; the shared-secret ops path has no "self" and is exempt, so it
can still recover any state);
* an unknown/anonymous id → 404 (only registered accounts have a role).

Handler: `handlers::admin::set_user_role_handler`

### `GET /api/admin/features`

GET /api/admin/features — every registered feature with its runtime state.

Handler: `handlers::admin::list_features_handler`

### `POST /api/admin/features/{key}`

POST /api/admin/features/{key} — set or clear a feature override. Unknown
keys are 404 (the registry lives in code; nothing to create).

Handler: `handlers::admin::set_feature_handler`

### `GET /api/admin/settings/{key}`

GET /api/admin/settings/{key} — the stored value of one registered setting.
Unknown keys are 404 (the registry lives in code; nothing to create).

Handler: `handlers::admin::get_setting_handler`

### `POST /api/admin/settings/{key}`

POST /api/admin/settings/{key} — set or clear a setting value. Unknown
keys are 404, like the feature-toggle mutation.

Handler: `handlers::admin::set_setting_handler`

### `GET /api/admin/stats`

GET /api/admin/stats — the admin analytics overview: KPI totals (+ previous
same-length window for bounded ranges), a zero-filled daily trend, and the
per-quest table over every published quest.

Handler: `handlers::admin::admin_stats_overview_handler`

### `GET /api/admin/stats/{quest_id}`

GET /api/admin/stats/{quest_id} — per-quest KPIs plus the step funnel over
the CURRENT published snapshot (labels are frozen per version).

Handler: `handlers::admin::admin_stats_quest_handler`

### `POST /api/migrate/legacy`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::admin::run_migration_handler`

### `POST /api/migrate/media`

POST /api/migrate/media — move the media of already-stored rows into the
media store (see [`backfill`]). Ops-token gated like the legacy migration:
it rewrites production content, and it is an operator action, not a product
feature. Idempotent and restartable; re-run while `complete` is false.

Handler: `handlers::admin::run_media_backfill_handler`

## `handlers::auth`

Account routes: register/login, social auth (Google/Telegram), identify/
recover/reset/confirm/resend/change-email (§6), account management
(display name, password, unlink, delete), linked-provider listing, and the
profile read.

### `POST /api/auth/register`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::auth::register_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/identify`

§6.1 — does this email have an account? Drives the single-form flow (the
409 «already registered» class disappears by construction). Rate-limited
per email (fixed window) — it is intentionally an existence oracle for the
form, so it must not become a cheap mass-enumeration endpoint.

Handler: `handlers::auth::identify_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/recover`

§6.2 — issue a password-reset link. The response is IDENTICAL whether or
not the email exists (no user enumeration). Reset links are only sent to
CONFIRMED emails; an unconfirmed account gets a fresh confirmation mail
instead (§6.3 — the UI explains this via identify.confirmed).

Handler: `handlers::auth::recover_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/reset`

§6.2 — consume the reset credential (link token or email-scoped code), set
the new password and SIGN IN (the flow ends with the user in their account,
per spec). Failures are ONE opaque 400 — wrong code, unknown email, expired
or spent credential are indistinguishable (no enumeration). Code guessing
is bounded by the store: `MAX_CODE_ATTEMPTS` per token, and recover itself
is mail-rate-limited, so no extra limiter is needed here.

Handler: `handlers::auth::reset_password_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/confirm`

One landing for both mailed links: a first-confirmation token stamps the
current address, an email-change token (§6.4) applies its pending NEW
address — proved reachable by this very click, so it lands confirmed.

Handler: `handlers::auth::confirm_email_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/confirm/resend`

§6.3 — resend the confirmation mail (Profile banner «Ещё раз»). Session-only.

Handler: `handlers::auth::resend_confirm_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/email`

§6.4 — request an email change (Profile «Изменить почту»). Session-only.
Nothing changes until the mailed link is opened FROM THE NEW ADDRESS —
that click both proves reachability and applies the change (see
[`confirm_email_handler`]). Also how a social-only account gains its first
address. The taken-address check up front is a UX courtesy; the store's
unique index stays the authority at apply time.

Handler: `handlers::auth::change_email_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/change-password`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::auth::change_password_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/display-name`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::auth::set_display_name_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/delete-account`

§7.4 — delete the account and its data, irreversibly. Editors with quests
still ON SALE are blocked (409): buyers keep access through the published
snapshot + grants, but an account that owns live store listings must delist
them first — otherwise the store would sell orphaned quests.

Handler: `handlers::auth::delete_account_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/login`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::auth::login_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/google`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::auth::google_auth_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/telegram`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::auth::telegram_auth_handler`

### `POST /api/auth/unlink`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::auth::unlink_handler`

### `GET /api/auth/providers`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

## `handlers::constructor`

Constructor dashboard routes — the authoring registry behind /quest-editor,
plus publish. Every endpoint is editor-gated (require_editor_actor: an
editor/admin session or the ops token). Completions ("прохождения") are derived per quest
from the fact log — never stored on the constructor row — so the metric stays
a pure projection.

### `POST /api/quests/publish`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::constructor::publish_quest_handler`

### `GET /api/constructor/quests`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::constructor::list_constructor_quests_handler`

### `POST /api/constructor/quests`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::constructor::create_constructor_quest_handler`

### `GET /api/constructor/quests/{quest_id}`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::constructor::get_constructor_quest_handler`

### `POST /api/constructor/quests/{quest_id}/save`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::constructor::save_constructor_quest_handler`

### `GET /api/constructor/authors`

GET /api/constructor/authors — who a quest may be transferred to: the accounts
that can author one ([`auth::role_can_author`]), admins first then editors,
alphabetical within a role. Admin-gated: this is the account registry, and the
transfer it feeds is an admin decision.

Handler: `handlers::constructor::list_authors_handler`

### `POST /api/constructor/quests/{quest_id}/status`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::constructor::set_constructor_status_handler`

### `POST /api/constructor/quests/{quest_id}/author`

POST /api/constructor/quests/{id}/author — hand the quest to another author.

Admin-only, because it is a change of access, not of content: the previous
author loses the quest outright. The target must be an account that can author
quests — handing one to a player would strand it where nobody may edit it.
Idempotent: transferring to the current owner is a no-op that still answers OK.

Handler: `handlers::constructor::set_constructor_author_handler`

### `POST /api/constructor/quests/{quest_id}/delete`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::constructor::delete_constructor_quest_handler`

### `GET /api/constructor/quests/{quest_id}/export`

GET /api/constructor/quests/{quest_id}/export — the full quest as a
downloadable zip: quest record (all steps, attributes, cover — media URLs
rewritten to point into the archive) and the media files themselves.
Content only — play/rating stats are live projections, not quest content.
Owner-or-admin gated, same as every other per-quest constructor route.

Handler: `handlers::constructor::export_constructor_quest_handler`

## `handlers::media`

Media routes: upload (editor-gated, lifts the body cap to a single image)
and the serve route (serves in-process AND R2 media through this origin).

### `POST /api/media`

POST /api/media — upload a quest image (editor-gated). The body is the raw
image bytes and `Content-Type` names the format. The SERVER hashes the bytes
(sha256) and stores them content-addressed in R2 (or the in-process store),
returning the public URL the quest JSON should reference. Idempotent: identical
bytes resolve to the same URL and are not re-stored.

Handler: `handlers::media::upload_media_handler`

### `GET /api/media/{hash}`

GET /api/media/{hash} — serve content-addressed media through the API's own
origin. Backs both stores: the in-process one (local dev / tests) and R2
(fetched from the bucket), so media is served without a public bucket domain.
A custom domain would instead serve R2 directly and this would 404 in prod.

Handler: `handlers::media::get_media_handler`

## `handlers::payments`

Payment routes: checkout, payment status/webhook settlement, provider
discovery, and the purchase-sheet coupon preview. Thin HTTP shims over
`crate::payments`.

### `POST /api/checkout`

Thin HTTP shim over [`payments::checkout`]: resolve the identity, then let
the payment module run the provider dispatch and coupon rules.

Handler: `handlers::payments::checkout_handler`

### `GET /api/payments/providers`

Providers this deployment can charge through — drives the purchase sheet's
payment-method choice (a single entry renders no selector; an empty list
disables paying). A provider is listed only when it is both configured
(capability) and switched on (feature toggle).

Handler: `handlers::payments::payment_providers_handler`

### `POST /api/payments/yookassa/webhook`

YooKassa HTTP notification. The body is only a pointer: settlement verifies
against the API, so a forged notification is harmless (and still gets 200).
Transient failures return 5xx so YooKassa keeps retrying (24h window).

Handler: `handlers::payments::yookassa_webhook_handler`

### `GET /api/payments/{payment_id}`

Owner poll for a redirect payment: lazily settles a still-pending row (the
return page lands here before the webhook on local/dev deployments).

Handler: `handlers::payments::payment_status_handler`

### `POST /api/coupons/validate`

Purchase-sheet promo preview: never mutates, always 200 with a verdict.
`{valid: true, ...}` carries the priced discount; `{valid: false, message}`
carries the player-facing reason (unknown and deleted codes read the same).

Handler: `handlers::payments::validate_coupon_handler`

## `handlers::player`

Player-facing routes: health probe, attempts + fact sync, bundle download,
marketplace catalog, product page, PWA icons, own grants, public feature
flags, measurement notes, and cross-attempt player stats.

### `GET /health`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::player::health_handler`

### `POST /api/attempts`

Creates an attempt for a grant holder, bound to the quest's latest published
snapshot (the binding never changes — version freeze). 401 for a registered
identity without a session, 403 without a grant, 404 for unpublished quests.

Handler: `handlers::player::create_attempt_handler`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

### `GET /api/quests/{quest_id}/bundle`

Bundle download primitive: latest frozen snapshot JSON, gated by grant/// Bundle download primitive: latest frozen snapshot JSON, gated by grant
(SPEC: "Grant before attempt/bundle"). Asset packing comes with the media
store phase.

Handler: `handlers::player::get_bundle_handler`

### `GET /api/quests/{quest_id}/bonuses`

What this quest has already paid the caller, on ANY of their devices — the
one thing a device that never played it cannot read out of its own storage.
The player asks before it plays and withholds these, so a replay is never
promised coins that are already banked (issue #117). Not access-gated: it
answers about the caller's own history and says nothing about the quest.

Handler: `handlers::player::get_quest_bonuses_handler`

### `GET /api/quests/{quest_id}`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::player::get_quest_product_handler`

### `GET /api/quests/{quest_id}/reviews`

GET /api/quests/{id}/reviews?offset=&limit= — visibility matches the
product page (published only).

Handler: `handlers::player::get_quest_reviews_handler`

### `GET /api/quests/{quest_id}/icons/{icon}`

§5/§12.7 — GET /api/quests/{id}/icons/{192|512}.png: the per-quest PWA
home-screen icon, composed from the published cover (center-crop, maskable
padding on brand navy). Immutable per published version — the manifest keys
the URL with ?v={snapshot_version}, so far-future caching is safe.

Handler: `handlers::player::get_quest_icon_handler`

### `GET /api/grants`

Grants for the resolved caller ONLY. Previously returned every player's
grants (incl. payment refs) to anyone — a cross-player data leak. The
marketplace/cabinet only ever need the caller's own ownership set.

Handler: `handlers::player::list_grants_handler`

### `GET /api/features`

GET /api/features — effective verdicts of the client-visible flags only
(`Feature::client_visible`). Public by design: the player runtime keys UI
behavior off these without credentials; server-enforced flags never appear.

Handler: `handlers::player::public_features_handler`

### `GET /api/measure/rates`

_No `///` on the handler — see the budget in `API.md`._

Handler: `handlers::player::get_measure_rates_handler`

### `GET /api/users/me/stats`

Cross-attempt player statistics: storage gathers the logs, the pure
projector folds them (player-stats spec; never re-folded in SQL).

Handler: `handlers::player::get_my_stats_handler`
